United States.text: The Soviet Union's collapse in 1991 left it as the world's sole superpower.
United States.evidence: The Soviet Union's collapse in 1991 left the U.S. as the world's sole superpower, although it has faced competition from China in the 2020s.

Soviet Union.text: It existed only from 1922 to 1991, and in that time was the largest country by area.
Soviet Union.evidence: The Soviet Union, officially the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR), was a transcontinental country that spanned much of Eurasia from its formation in 1922 until its dissolution in 1991. It was the world's third-most populous country, the largest by area, and bordered twelve other countries.

Great Britain.text: Until 9,000 years ago it was joined to mainland Europe by a land bridge now called Doggerland.
Great Britain.evidence: Connected to mainland Europe until 9,000 years ago by a land bridge now known as Doggerland, the island of Great Britain has been inhabited by modern humans for around 30,000 years.

France.text: The kingdom grew out of West Francia, split off from the Carolingian Empire by the Treaty of Verdun in 843.
France.evidence: The Treaty of Verdun of 843 partitioned the empire, with West Francia evolving into the Kingdom of France.

Germany.text: It is both the world's third-largest exporter and its third-largest importer.
Germany.evidence: As a major force in several industrial, scientific and technological sectors, Germany is both the world's third-largest exporter and third-largest importer.

Italy.text: Two other countries sit entirely inside it: Vatican City and San Marino.
Italy.evidence: Italy shares land borders with France to the west; Switzerland and Austria to the north; Slovenia to the east; and the two enclaves of Vatican City and San Marino.

China.text: Unified under the Qin in 221 BCE, it went on to two millennia of imperial rule.
China.evidence: In 221 BCE, China was unified under the Qin, followed by the Han dynasty, ushering in two millennia of imperial rule across periods of unity and division.

Sweden.text: Its last war was in 1814, when it forced Norway into a union that lasted until 1905.
Sweden.evidence: The last war in which Sweden was directly involved was in 1814, when Sweden by military means forced Norway into a personal union, a union which lasted until 1905.

Japan.text: An American fleet forced it to open trade to the West in 1853, which led to the end of the shogunate.
Japan.evidence: In 1853, an American fleet forced Japan to open trade to the West, which led to the end of the shogunate and the restoration of imperial power in 1868.

Australia.text: It is the world's flattest and driest inhabited continent.
Australia.evidence: It has a land area of 7,688,287 km2 (2,968,464 sq mi), making it the sixth-largest country in the world, and is the world's flattest and driest inhabited continent.
